title: The Vitality Edge: How Large-Cap CEOs Keep Reinventing Growth
gist: BCG Henderson Institute's 2026 Vitality Index, built from 15 weighted metrics across ~3,500 companies, finds that above-median-vitality firms outgrew peers by 5.2 points of annual revenue growth and that firms which improved vitality earned 6.8 points more annual TSR; the report profiles 25 large-cap vitality leaders (L'Oréal, MercadoLibre, Tesla, Apple, Eaton, and others) and distills five actions CEOs take to build it.

themes.theme: The Vitality Index: Methodology and Predictive Power

insights.claim: BCG's 2026 Vitality Index assessed more than 3,500 public and private companies over a five-year period, testing over 30 variables for statistical significance and drawing on roughly 10 million data points (including Revelio Labs workforce data and HG Insights tech-quality data) to build a composite score from 15 weighted metrics tied to long-term revenue growth.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Investors can treat the vitality score as a systematic, forward-looking screen for future growth and TSR outperformance rather than relying on trailing financial metrics.

insights.claim: Companies with above-median vitality scores achieved annual revenue growth 5.2 percentage points higher over the following five years than companies with lower vitality scores.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: A 5.2pp annual growth gap compounds materially over five years, making vitality score a candidate screening factor for growth-oriented equity selection.
insights.quote: Companies with above-median scores in our study achieved annual revenue growth that was 5.2 percentage points higher over the ensuing five years than that of their less vital peers.
insights.locator: The rewards of improving vitality are substantial

insights.claim: Companies that started with low vitality but improved it over the study period earned an additional 6.8 percentage points in annual total shareholder return compared with the rest of the companies studied.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Improving vitality trajectory, not just current level, is itself a TSR-relevant signal — investors can look for firms with rising vitality scores even from a low base.
insights.quote: Companies that started with low vitality but improved it over the same period earned an additional 6.8 percentage points in annual total shareholder return (TSR) compared to the rest of the companies in the study.
insights.locator: The rewards of improving vitality are substantial

insights.claim: One in three companies in the study raised their vitality score by at least 10 percentage points relative to industry peers, showing vitality is a management lever that can be deliberately moved, not a fixed trait.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Because vitality is improvable at a granular level, a sudden vitality jump can serve as an early signal of a turnaround before it shows up in reported financials.
insights.locator: No CEO needs to settle for low vitality

insights.claim: From 2024 to 2026, the share of corporate innovation budgets allocated to core initiatives rose 12 percentage points while investment in adjacent and transformational bets declined, as higher capital costs and intensified investor scrutiny of ROI pushed companies to resize noncore initiatives.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: A structural shift toward core-focused capex means investors should expect fewer moonshot bets and more capital-disciplined reinvestment in existing business lines across large caps.
insights.quote: the share of innovation budgets allocated to core initiatives increased by 12 percentage points while investment in adjacent and transformational bets declined
insights.locator: Five Actions That CEOs Can Take to Increase Vitality (intro)

insights.claim: Among companies with market caps above $25 billion, those in the top vitality quartile achieved 11.5% annual revenue growth over five years versus a 6.6% average for large companies overall, and generated annual TSR 3.1 percentage points higher than large companies in the bottom vitality quartile.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Even among mega-caps where growth is typically assumed to plateau, top-quartile vitality still nearly doubles revenue growth versus the large-cap average — a screenable gap for growth investors.
insights.quote: those in the highest vitality quartile achieved 11.5% annual revenue growth over five years, compared with an average of 6.6% for large companies overall.
insights.locator: The growth flywheel is especially valuable for large enterprises

themes.theme: The Vitality Flywheel: Three Reinforcing Traits

insights.claim: BCG's vitality framework reduces to three reinforcing traits measured through 15 biomarkers: High Growth Ambition (bold targets backed by capital allocation and incentives), High Talent Density (growth teams with the skills, mobility, and experience to scale new businesses), and Growth-Centric Culture (low bureaucracy, lean management, and AI/tech adoption).
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Gives investors a structured checklist to evaluate management quality beyond financial statements when assessing a company's durable growth potential.

insights.claim: No company reaches high vitality by excelling in only one of the three traits; ambition attracts strong talent, which raises talent density and pushes the culture to reinvent itself, which in turn builds leaders' confidence to raise ambition further, forming a self-reinforcing flywheel.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Single-lever turnarounds (e.g., just cutting bureaucracy, or just raising R&D spend) are unlikely to move the needle — investors should be skeptical of companies claiming a one-dimensional growth fix.
insights.locator: No company becomes highly vital by excelling in just one of these areas

insights.claim: Top vitality performers are nearly ten times as likely as low performers to rank in the top quartile on at least one variable across all three core vitality capabilities (growth ambition, talent density, and culture) simultaneously.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Balanced strength across all three dimensions, not depth in one, is the statistically differentiating trait of elite vitality companies — a useful qualitative filter for stock screening.
insights.quote: top vitality performers are nearly ten times as likely as low performers to rank in the top quartile on at least one variable across all three core vitality capabilities.

insights.claim: Several of the 15 vitality biomarkers are built from unconventional data sources: Minimum Viable Bureaucracy is scored from the share of Glassdoor reviews mentioning terms like "red tape" or "complexity," and Growth Incentives is an LLM-based score of how long-term incentive structures are described in executive pay disclosures.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Alternative-data signals like employee review sentiment and NLP-scored pay incentives can be tracked independently by investors as proxies for organizational health between earnings reports.

themes.theme: Sector Playbooks: Which Levers Matter Where

insights.claim: Aerospace and defense shows the greatest cross-industry mobility in vitality of any sector studied — individual companies (spotlighting Axon Enterprise) can climb from a low base to the top quintile within five years even though the industry's overall average vitality score is below average, with human capital (innovator tenure, workforce stability, growth experience) mattering more than financial capital deployed.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: A below-average sector average shouldn't deter stock-pickers from individual aerospace/defense names — the dispersion means specific companies can re-rate quickly on talent-driven vitality gains.

insights.claim: In automotive, vitality builders (spotlighting Tesla) out-innovate peers in the EV transition mainly through internal R&D momentum, workforce stability, and reduced bureaucracy, while struggling automakers show vitality declines led entirely by organizational erosion (falling innovator tenure, growth ambition, and lean management) that precedes any external loss of market share.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Organizational metrics (headcount stability, management layers, tenure) can serve as leading indicators of automaker underperformance before it shows up in delivery or market-share numbers.

insights.claim: In construction and engineering, growth experience — hiring leaders from high-growth companies — is the single largest vitality lever of any industry in the study, with Larsen & Toubro spotlighted, while the sector's persistent structural weakness is a digital-capability gap.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Watch executive-hiring patterns at construction/engineering firms — poaching leaders from fast-growing companies is the strongest observable signal of a coming vitality (and growth) improvement.

insights.claim: In consumer durables and apparel, capital advantage (price-to-book ratio) is both the top vitality signal and the largest lever for improvement, spotlighting Hermès, as tariffs and more selective consumers squeeze mid-tier brand loyalty even as luxury demand keeps surging.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Supports a barbell view of consumer durables investing: premium/luxury names with strong price-to-book keep compounding while mid-tier apparel brands face structural pressure.

insights.claim: In metals and mining, despite the sector having the most capex-centric leader profile in the study given its capital intensity, vitality builders (spotlighting Wheaton Precious Metals) gain most from R&D momentum, treating mining as a materials-and-process innovation business with above-peer patented process innovation rather than pure commodity extraction.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Mining companies investing in process/technology patents, not just capex on new capacity, may be under-recognized vitality gainers as critical-minerals demand rises.

insights.claim: Pharma and biotech shows the widest gap between top and median vitality performers of any industry studied — leaders reach exceptional scores while the typical company sits near zero — indicating the vitality playbook (led by innovator tenure and workforce stability, spotlighting Natera) is well defined but not widely adopted across the sector.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: The wide top-to-median dispersion in pharma vitality suggests high alpha potential in identifying the small set of biotech/pharma names actually executing the talent-retention playbook.

insights.claim: Semiconductors have the largest gap between top performers and the rest of any industry in the study; vitality builders (spotlighting Astera Labs) climb primarily through innovator tenure and workforce stability — retaining top engineers through downcycles — rather than through the biggest capex budgets.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: In semis, engineer-retention metrics through downcycles may be a better forward-looking signal of competitive position than headline capex or fab investment announcements.

insights.claim: Software and services is the only industry in the study where even bottom-quartile companies post positive vitality scores, and leadership within the sector (spotlighting Snowflake) is defined less by spend than by who firms hire — innovator tenure, AI fluency, and digital edge weigh nearly as heavily as capital advantage.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Software's uniformly positive vitality floor implies the sector deserves a structurally higher growth-multiple baseline versus other industries, all else equal.

insights.claim: In retail, workforce stability is the single dominant vitality lever, spotlighting MercadoLibre, driving both vitality gains and vitality declines — in a frontline-heavy industry where institutional knowledge sits at the store level, reducing voluntary attrition is the key growth lever available to CEOs.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Employee-attrition data at retailers can be tracked as a proxy for future same-store growth momentum, ahead of reported comps.

insights.claim: Transportation shows the largest within-industry mobility of any sector in the dataset, spotlighting Ryanair, with top vitality builders gaining about 46 percentile points relative to peers through a combination of growth experience, innovator tenure, workforce stability, and AI adoption, with no single dominant playbook.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: The scale of achievable within-sector re-ranking (46 percentile points) means transportation names can re-rate sharply on operational execution alone, independent of macro fuel or travel-demand cycles.

themes.theme: Regional and Structural Divergence Across Industries

insights.claim: Utilities show the sharpest regional split in the entire vitality dataset, with North America well above Asia, Latin America, and Europe, as spotlighted by Vistra amid a new demand-growth cycle driven by data centers, AI infrastructure, and electrification.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: US power/utility names tied to data-center and AI-infrastructure buildout look structurally better positioned on vitality than non-US utility peers.

insights.claim: Telecom is a rare case where North America trails the rest of the group in vitality, spotlighting SoftBank, suggesting the most vital telecom operators sit outside the saturated US market, even as the sector shows an unusually innovation-heavy profile (anchored in innovator tenure and R&D momentum) for a capital-intensive industry.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Investors defaulting to US telecom incumbents as the sector's quality leaders should reconsider — non-US operators may be the more vital, better-positioned names.

insights.claim: In consumer services, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa trails the rest of the group by 17 percentile points, a sharper regional split than most other industries, while the sector's distinctive vitality lever (spotlighting Viking Holdings) is R&D momentum — unusual for a services industry and a sign firms are repositioning as technology businesses with consumer-facing surfaces.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Consumer-services companies investing in R&D/technology like a software business, not just loyalty programs, are the ones likely to outrun EMEA's structural vitality gap.

insights.claim: In chemicals and materials, Asian firms are systematically more vital than European peers, spotlighting Sherwin-Williams, a regional gap BCG frames as a strategic issue CEOs should resolve directly rather than a cyclical artifact.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: European chemicals names may carry a structural vitality discount versus Asian peers that isn't fully priced into relative valuations.

themes.theme: Five Actions CEOs Take to Build Vitality

insights.claim: Vitality leaders move innovation from the edge to the core: rather than relying on incubators, venture funds, digital labs, and corporate venture capital disconnected from the main business, they treat the core business itself as the primary innovation engine and expect every business unit to identify, build, and scale new sources of growth.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Companies announcing large standalone venture arms or innovation labs disconnected from core operations may be following a less effective playbook than those embedding innovation directly in existing business units.
insights.locator: Move from the Edge to the Core

insights.claim: Eaton, a century-old power management company, improved its vitality score by 50 percentage points over five years by divesting noncore businesses (lighting, hydraulics, and a planned mobility divestiture) and reinvesting in higher-growth opportunities, and delivered 23.9% annual TSR over the period versus a 13.4% industry median.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Eaton's near-2x TSR outperformance versus its industry median demonstrates that portfolio pruning toward the core, not diversification, can be the dominant driver of vitality and shareholder return.
insights.quote: During the same period, Eaton delivered 23.9% annual TSR, compared with the industry median of 13.4%.
insights.locator: Move from the Edge to the Core

insights.claim: Vitality leaders measure vitality with the same discipline applied to revenue, margins, and cash flow, monitoring all 15 underlying variables across the three vitality traits continuously so they can adjust course before small gaps become large ones, rather than waiting for financial results to reveal whether today's decisions are working.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Companies that disclose or track granular workforce/innovation KPIs alongside financials may be better positioned to catch growth deterioration earlier than peers relying solely on quarterly numbers.
insights.locator: Measure Vitality Like Any Other Critical KPI

insights.claim: Because vitality cuts across the whole enterprise rather than belonging to any single innovation, R&D, or strategy function, vitality leaders assign a clear executive owner — the CEO, CFO, or chief strategy officer — with a common fact base to align investment decisions and hold the organization accountable.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: The presence (or absence) of a named executive owner for growth/innovation metrics can be a useful qualitative diligence flag when evaluating management quality.

insights.claim: The most vital companies don't try to improve all 15 biomarkers at once; they identify the few most likely to constrain future growth in their specific competitive context and concentrate leadership attention and investment there.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Companies pursuing a broad, unfocused set of transformation initiatives simultaneously may be less effective than those making a small number of targeted, high-conviction bets.
insights.locator: Identify and Close the Most Important Vitality Gaps

insights.claim: L'Oréal climbed 26 percentile points over five years to become the large-cap vitality leader in beauty by concentrating on capital advantage and modern tech stacks, backed by more than €1.3 billion in annual R&D spending — which the company describes as the largest research effort in the cosmetics industry — plus targeted digital investments such as its CreAItech content lab and Cell BioPrint lab-on-a-chip diagnostic device.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: L'Oréal's targeted R&D and digital-innovation spend (CreAItech, Cell BioPrint) illustrates a concrete, replicable template for consumer-products peers seeking to lift vitality without diffusing investment across every lever.
insights.quote: which L'Oréal describes as the largest research effort in the cosmetics industry
insights.locator: Identify and Close the Most Important Vitality Gaps

themes.theme: Proof Point: Embedding Vitality in Enterprise Transformation

insights.claim: Vitality leaders use the vitality framework as an organizing principle for enterprise transformation itself, ensuring growth ambition, talent density, and growth-centric culture reinforce one another rather than compete for attention, instead of treating vitality-building as just another standalone transformation initiative.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: Transformation programs that address culture, talent, and growth strategy as one integrated effort are more likely to sustain vitality gains than siloed cost-cutting or reorganization initiatives.

insights.claim: MercadoLibre sustained a 98th-percentile vitality score within its industry in 2026 even while growing in scale, by supporting its core e-commerce and fintech business with targeted bolt-on expansion into fintech, logistics, advertising, and AI-powered services, building the teams, technology, and operating capabilities to scale those businesses together rather than treating new products as isolated bets.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/ketil-gjerstad
insights.so_what: MercadoLibre's ability to hold a top-percentile vitality score while scaling suggests its bolt-on fintech/logistics/advertising expansion strategy is a durable growth model rather than a one-off cycle, supporting continued premium multiple justification.
